name: similar-shapes-table
title: Similar shapes measurements table
tagline: Two or three similar shapes compared in a working table — shapes as columns, Length / Area / Volume as rows, with derived ×k / ×k² / ×k³ scale-factor arrows across the gaps.
description: Two or three similar shapes compared in a working table: the shapes are the columns (Shape A, Shape B, optionally Shape C) and Length, Area and Volume are the rows, each cell holding a shape's actual measurement, with ×k / ×k² / ×k³ scale-factor arrows running across the gap between shape columns — one per row, because lengths scale by k, areas by k² and volumes by k³. You write the reference shape's measurements (its length, and optionally its area and volume) and, for each other shape, either its linear scale factor k or one known corresponding measurement; the model derives every other measurement (reference × k / k² / k³), the per-row factors, and an optional working strip. Occlude any measurement to "?" for "find the missing length / area / volume" and "given the area ratio, find the volume", highlight the answer in amber, hide the factors for "what is the area scale factor?", and add a base unit so the rows read cm / cm² / cm³. The concrete, measurement-bearing partner to geometry/similarity-ratio-table (which shows only the abstract k / k² / k³) and the geometry/similar-shapes figure.
whenToUse: Reach for this to compare two or three similar shapes by their actual measurements in a table — Shape A, B (and C) down the columns, Length / Area / Volume down the rows — with the ×k / ×k² / ×k³ relationship shown across the columns. This is the figure for "Shape A has length 5 cm and area 20 cm²; Shape B is similar with length 15 cm — find its area", and for "the volumes of two similar solids are 8 and 216; find the ratio of their surface areas". Author a `shapes` array: the first shape is the reference — give its `length` (required) and optionally `area` and `volume` (a row shows only if the reference has it); each later shape gives either `scale` (its linear scale factor k) or `known` ({ of, value } — one corresponding measurement, to back-derive k). You never write a derived shape's measurements — length × k, area × k², volume × k³ are all computed. Common configurations: worked — give scale, show.working true to reveal "Area ×k² = 3² = 9"; find a missing measure — occlude a cell (e.g. shape 2 area) and highlight it, giving the scaffold (the lengths + the other areas) in the visible cells; area / volume ratio — give a shape via known area or known volume and occlude another row; what is the area scale factor — show.factors false so the arrows read "× ?"; blank table — occlude every derived cell. Add `unit` (e.g. "cm") so the rows read Length (cm) / Area (cm²) / Volume (cm³). Keep k rational (a scale, a known length, or a perfect-square area / perfect-cube volume ratio) — for surd scale-factor reasoning on the abstract k / k² / k³ relationship use geometry/similarity-ratio-table instead. Switch model: to draw the two similar shapes with marked corresponding sides use geometry/similar-shapes; for the abstract scale-factor-only table (no real measurements) use geometry/similarity-ratio-table; for a generic ratio/proportion table use number/ratio-table. Strongly staged: open on the reference column with the others blank, bring in the per-row factors, then the derived cells. Synonyms a teacher might use: similar shapes, similar solids, scale factor, area scale factor, volume scale factor, k squared, k cubed, ratio of areas, ratio of volumes, find the missing area, find the volume, corresponding lengths, enlargement.

items.description: One shape = one COLUMN, left to right. The FIRST shape is the REFERENCE: give its actual measurements (`length` required, `area` / `volume` optional — a row appears only if the reference has that measure). Every LATER shape is DERIVED from the reference: give EITHER `scale` (its linear scale factor k) OR `known` (one corresponding measurement, to back-derive k) — never its raw measurements.

name.description: Column header for this shape — "Shape A", "P", "Small". Defaults to "Shape A", "Shape B", … by position.

length.description: REFERENCE shape only: its length (a side, height, …). Required on the first shape; the Length row is always shown. Ignored on a derived shape (its length = reference length × k).

area.description: REFERENCE shape only: its area. Optional — give it to show the Area row. Ignored on a derived shape (area = reference area × k²).

volume.description: REFERENCE shape only: its volume. Optional — give it to show the Volume row. Ignored on a derived shape (volume = reference volume × k³).

scale.description: DERIVED shape only: the LINEAR scale factor k from the reference to this shape (3 → lengths ×3, areas ×9, volumes ×27; 0.5 → ÷2; 2.5 stays exact). Use this OR `known`, not both (scale wins).

known.description: DERIVED shape only: ONE known corresponding measurement of this shape, used to BACK-DERIVE k (k = known length ÷ reference length, √(known area ÷ reference area), or ∛(known volume ÷ reference volume)). The classic "given a length / area, find the rest". Keep k rational (a length, or a perfect-square area / perfect-cube volume ratio).

of.description: Which measure the known value is — "length", "area" or "volume".

value.description: This shape's value for that measure.

shapes.description: The shape columns, left to right (two or three). Item 0 is the REFERENCE (give its measurements); items 1+ are DERIVED (give `scale` or `known`).

unit.description: Optional base length unit, e.g. "cm", "m", "mm". The row labels become Length (cm) / Area (cm²) / Volume (cm³); cells stay bare numbers. Omit for unitless rows.

items.description: A per-cell question / emphasis flag. The cell's value is always computed; list it here only to occlude ("?") or amber it.

shape.description: Which shape COLUMN, 1-based (1 = the reference / first shape).

occlude.description: Render this measurement as "?" — the "find the missing measurement" hook. It appears nowhere else, so it cannot leak. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this measurement — answer emphasis. Default false.

cells.description: Per-cell occlusion / highlight overrides, addressed by `shape` (1-based column) and `measure` (row). Values are always computed; list a cell only to hide ("?") or amber it.

factors.description: Show the numeric scale factor on each row's arrow (×3, ×9, ×27). Default true. Set false to pose "what do you multiply by?" — the arrows read "× ?".

working.description: Show the derivation strip beneath the table — how k is found and how each row's factor follows ("Length ×3; Area ×3² = 9; Volume ×3³ = 27"). Occlusion-aware (a hidden value shows "?"). Use on worked examples. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the table; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the table, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
